eggNOG 4,5 has improved functional annotation of eukaryotic and prokaryotic proteins and added a new data set for viral proteins.
we provide a hierarchical framework for functional annotation of eukaryotic (including human) and prokaryotic proteins and viruses.
we have improved the eggNOG resource with a hierarchical orthology algorithm, new functional annotations and a novel viral data set.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of bioinformatics tools and databases to the analysis of genomic data, with a special emphasis on comparative genomics and phylogenetics.
the development and maintenance of a comprehensive resource for orthologous groups and the functional annotation of proteins across the tree of life.
the development of new methods and software for the analysis of protein sequences, with a focus on functional annotation, evolutionary inference and the integration of heterogeneous data.

eggNOG 4,5 is a great resource that is very well suited for comparative genomics studies.
eggNOG v 4.5 is a major upgrade of eggNOG that provides a wealth of information and new tools to facilitate the study of gene and protein function across all of life.
eggNOG 4 is a very useful tool for orthology analysis and functional annotation of protein families.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
eggNOG is now the largest resource of orthologous proteins with integrated and summarized annotations, covering all domains of life.
we have developed a resource that facilitates functional annotation of novel proteins and that is useful for comparative genomics and evolutionary studies.
we have improved eggNOG in all aspects, including its content and the way it can be accessed.

a hierarchical framework for the annotation of protein sequences, such as eggNOG, can be used to improve functional annotations of novel sequences.
the functional annotation of proteins can be greatly improved through the integration of orthology relationships across a wide range of taxonomic levels.
the eggNOG framework can now provide a more comprehensive view of the functional annotations of the proteome of an organism.
